text:
Simon Holmstrom's month has a plot. Yahoo Sports wrote about him showing what he can do after a demotion to the fourth line, and on Nov. 14 in Anaheim he scored his first NHL hat trick and got the Islanders' postgame oar for it. He has a five-game point streak (five goals, four assists) and 16 points in 20 games, after 0.52 points a game last season.

Our breakout check likes the shape of it. He's playing 18:07 a night, up from 16:44, he's on the ice for 46% of the Islanders' power-play chances (19% last season), and his own chances are up to 0.94 expected goals per 60 from 0.66. Evolving-Hockey also had him drawing more penalties than he takes, worth about two goals last season.

The finishing is the part to discount. Nine goals on 5.7 expected, shooting 25% against 19% last season, and the Islanders have scored 5.8 more goals than expected with him on. He'll cool off. What looks real is the role, and a heavier shot (96th percentile in top speed) getting more chances to fire.
